name: PCV (Procarbazine / Lomustine / Vincristine)

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Central Nervous System Cancers (general reference)

institution.provenance: DRAFT decision-support protocol authored from standard guidelines (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: lomustine day is high-to-moderate emetic risk; give a 5-HT3 antagonist (and consider a longer-acting agent) before the lomustine dose and before procarbazine days.

supportiveCare: Procarbazine is a weak MAO inhibitor: counsel on avoiding tyramine-rich foods and interacting drugs/alcohol during procarbazine days.
Delayed and cumulative myelosuppression from the nitrosourea (lomustine): the 6-week cycle length reflects the late count nadir - do not shorten it.
Vincristine is a vesicant given by slow IV push; monitor for peripheral neuropathy and constipation.
monitoring: CBC before each cycle and at the expected nadir (weeks 4-6 for lomustine)
Liver and renal function before each cycle
Neurologic exam for vincristine neuropathy; hold or reduce for significant neuropathy

drugs.name: Lomustine (CCNU)
drugs.notes: 110 mg/m2 by mouth once on day 1 of each 6-week (42-day) cycle. Nitrosourea backbone; expect delayed marrow nadir, so cycles are spaced 6 weeks apart (NCCN CNS / DeVita, general reference; own wording).

drugs.name: Procarbazine
drugs.notes: 60 mg/m2 by mouth once daily on days 8 to 21 of each 6-week cycle. MAO-inhibitor dietary precautions apply during dosing (NCCN CNS / DeVita, general reference; own wording).

drugs.name: Vincristine
drugs.notes: 1.4 mg/m2 IV push on days 8 and 29 of each 6-week cycle, capped at 2 mg per dose. Vesicant; hold/reduce for grade 2+ neuropathy (NCCN CNS / DeVita, general reference; own wording).
